title: Target pairs recurred at synapses above fixed-count control means in eight worm brain maps
abstract: We tested whether target pairs occur together at repeated chemical synapses more often than fixed connection counts predict. We used eight public C. elegans brain maps and a fixed panel of 162 neurons. Within each source cell, controls kept each target count and the number of targets at each site. The observed repeated-pair score was 1.61 to 2.18 times the mean of 398 control samples per map. All eight scores were above the control means. These results describe target grouping that a count-weighted edge table does not specify. Geometry and local contact limits were not controlled. The samples used finite randomization chains. No neural activity was tested. The result does not establish shared noise, a developmental trend, or transfer to other species.

display.caption: Observed repeated target-pair scores and the fixed-margin control distributions in eight worm brain maps.
